feature: Picking a layer brings its own section into view
summary: Click a piece of text, a measurement or a zoom callout and the right hand panel now scrolls itself so that thing's own settings are on screen. Before, on a marked up screenshot in a laptop window, the Text section sat 70 points below the bottom of the panel and you had to find it with the scroll wheel.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, a 1200 by 720 window. Nothing to turn on; this is how the panel behaves now.

try.do: Open a screenshot and mark it up until the layers list is full: four rectangles, an arrow, a measurement, a piece of text and a zoom callout.
Click the text layer in the layers list on the right.
Read the Text section at the bottom of the panel without touching the scroll wheel.
Click the measurement layer and read its Measurement section the same way.
Click the arrow layer, whose Arrow section already fits, and watch that the panel does not move.
Click a plain rectangle and watch that the panel does not move either.
Click the text layer again, scroll the panel back to the top by hand, then click the zoom callout.

evaluate: When the panel scrolls itself, does it land where your eye expected, or does it feel like the panel jumped?
Picking a text layer scrolls the layers list off the top of the panel. Does losing the list you just clicked in bother you more than not seeing the Text settings did?
The section it scrolls to sits flush against the bottom edge of the panel. Should it stop a little short of the edge instead?
Clicking a plain rectangle leaves the panel exactly where it was. Should a rectangle pull the panel back to the top instead of leaving it wherever the last pick put it?
Drawing a new zoom callout also scrolls the panel to its settings. Is that welcome, or noise in the middle of drawing?
rough: The real cost, and it is unavoidable: the panel holds about 1030 points of sections in a 690 point window, so showing the Text section means the layers list goes off the top. You click a row and the list of rows leaves. Nothing can show both.

The top of the panel is then an orphan: the first thing you see is a colour row with no heading above it, because the scroll cut Appearance in half. That is true of any scrolled panel, but this makes it happen more often.

Clicking empty canvas deliberately does NOT scroll to the Canvas section. Putting something down is not the same as asking about the canvas, and a panel that jumped on every deselect would be jumping most of the time.
A collapsed section is scrolled to as a header and left collapsed. Opening it for you would undo a choice you made on purpose.
Picking the same layer twice does nothing, so scrolling away by hand and clicking the same row again will not bring the section back. Clicking a different layer and back does.
